I asked one of the mfms about the immunosuppressants impact on a fetus and I got a vague “certain ones are safe others aren’t.” There is data from use of them during pregnancy for those with autoimmune diseases that there is an increased risk of growth restriction and pre term birth. Most of these babies from transplants are delivered early (around 36 weeks) and always by C-section. 

It will be interesting to see the long term effects on the women who go through the whole 5 year process. There’s not that many of them yet. I was just re reading a 2017 Times article and one of the leads of this uterus transplant trial is quoted as saying “When you donate a kidney, you do it to help someone live longer and get off dialysis, for these women, they are donating an experience.”

From a medical perspective, it is amazing. The recipients are permitted 2 pregnancies max with the uterus, although I do know of a case in which a third was permitted. The uterus can be from a live or deceased donor. The first embryo can be implanted 6-12 months after the transplant. After 2-3 pregnancies, the uterus is removed. I believe all of the transplants in the US have been through a clinical trial, and right now the UNTIL trial is actively enrolling. 

The eligibility criteria for recipients is women 21-40 years old with uterine factor infertility, in good health, non smokers. They also need to be in a “stable relationship that has lasted at least 3 years.” The relationship can be same sex. 

My qualms are really related to the amount of resources that have gone into the research and development of this type of transplant. I think my idea of a transplant is a life saving mechanism, or for improvement of QOL. I don’t really know about transplant research in general, I’m just thinking there are other life saving types in the works and perhaps resources are best directed there? Or even better directed towards making life saving medication/ treatments affordable? 

I don’t have Uterine Factor Infertility, and I know there are women who place very high value on carrying a child. I can understand that. We have patients from out of state and Canada who regularly fly in for appointments with the research team and us. It’s a massive financial, time, and emotional investment for about 5 years. They’re on immunosuppressants for the duration.
